facts.raw_span: A 54-year-old woman
living in upstate New York
medical history significant for idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL) originally diagnosed in 2015
with an annual CD4 cell count ranging between 14 and 18 cells/µL
She initially presented to her primary care physician with a sore throat
no systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, myalgias) or pulmonary symptoms
Laryngoscopy revealed thickening of the epiglottic mucosa with irregularity and white plaques
A repeat laryngoscopy demonstrated progression of the plaques
Laryngeal cultures initially grew Streptococcus mitis, Streptococcus salivarius, Rothia mucilaginosus, Neisseria flavescens/subflava, and Candida albicans
Urine histoplasma antigen: positive at 0.3 ng/mL
Laryngeal biopsy revealed rare hyphae and yeast forms on Grocott methenamine silver stain with no evidence of malignancy or granulomas
Fungal culture grew Histoplasma capsulatum, identified by typical tuberculate microconidia
